summary: A tight economic puzzle where players bid for power plants, buy resources on a shared market, and build networks of cities, but only the plants you can actually fuel and power at payout matter. Turn order rotates so the leader goes last in every phase except paying the most for plants, creating a self-balancing catch-up mechanism that keeps games close until the end.
praised: Elegant self-balancing turn order that keeps the game close
Deep economic tension between expanding, buying plants, and stockpiling resources
High replayability from variable maps, plant decks, and player counts
Rewards efficient planning and resource management
criticised: Long playtime, especially with 5-6 players due to auction and bidding phases
Downtime waiting for other players' turns, particularly the auction phase
Can feel unforgiving to new players who fall behind early
Theme is dry/abstract for some tastes
Fixed endgame trigger can lead to anticlimactic finishes
win_criteria: Most points, one or two sources

scoring.why: The winner is whoever can power the most cities when someone's network hits the end-game size threshold.
